text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Criminal police in Tallinn discovered an underground printing plant that produced U.S. dollars, drivers licences and excise stamps, police officials said.
- Why did Borje Strenstrom, a Swedish member of the Estonia investigation commission who died a month ago, send three letters and the report to the German shipbuilder Meyer-Werft, the newspaper asks.
- The police continue to check the loads of trucks. A total 483 overloaded lorries have been discovered in the three months of 1997, police officials said.
- A maximum 100,000 tickets would be sold for Michael Jackson's concert in Tallinn in August, organisers said.
- The Moderate Party re-elected Andres Tarand as chairman at a congress on April 19.
- The parliament Chechen support group will hold meetings in Tallinn and Tartu today to commemorate the death of Dzokar Dudayev a year ago.
- Shareholders of Tallinn Department Store approved at a meeting on April 19 doubling the share capital from 33.9 million kroons to 67,8 million kroons.
- Arvo Sirendi was re-elected as chairman of the Rural Union at a congress on April 19.
- Hansapank will double its stock with a new issue of shares on April 28. The share price is expected to fall 50 percent to take account of the new new shares on the market.
